title: Finite-projective determinant module as an exterior-algebra socle
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $E$ an $R$-module. Using the exterior algebra and its canonical map $\iota_E$ [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], define the $R$-submodule $D_R(E)=\{x\in\bigwedge_R(E):x\wedge\iota_E(e)=0\text{ for every }e\in E\}$. For a finite projective module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] this is the socle model of its determinant module, denoted $\det_R(E)$. For a commutative $R$-algebra $A$, an $A$-module $F$ with compatible restricted $R$-action and an $R$-linear map $f:E\to F$, define $\bigwedge f:\bigwedge_R(E)\to\bigwedge_A(F)$ as the unique $R$-algebra map taking $\iota_E(e)$ to $\iota_F(f(e))$. In particular this is the exterior-algebra map used on localization charts.

The wedge formula covers all bases, tuples and lifts, Fin 0 included; the localization square is checked by naturality on ι-generators. Hypotheses are exactly Finite+Projective, injective, surjective, Exact; universes are independent; edge cases R=0, zero modules, varying rank and char 2 are fine. The new node def-trf-projective-determinant-module matches the source and the §5 field list, has real data, and duplicates nothing in the side DAG, Sheaf or Mathlib (the sc sheaf determinant is constant-rank).
